collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 5-12)

collection.description: A child hears an adult tell how a knee-high wave was taller than a hut: speak up, or say nothing.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: This morning (subject) rode a wave into the beach on a flat piece of driftwood. By lunchtime, as (subject.he/she) tells it to a little crowd, the wave was taller than a hut. (friend), who was sitting on the beach when it happened, has just wandered over to listen. (friend) remembers a wave about as tall as a knee.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "It was this big," says (friend), holding a hand at knee height. Everyone looks at (subject). "From where you were sitting," says (subject). "From where I was, it was enormous." (friend) thinks about this and decides that's fair. Waves probably do look bigger when you're on them.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) says nothing and listens. The wave gets bigger. Now there was a second wave, even bigger. (friend) giggles. Afterward (subject) catches (friend.his/her) eye and winks. That afternoon they go down to the beach together, and (subject) teaches (friend) to ride a knee-sized wave, which turns out to be quite exciting enough.
